description: We are a multidisciplinary team of six united by our passion for science, technology, and innovation. Bringing together expertise in physics, computer science, mechanical engineering, electronics, automation, mechatronics, and production programming, we combine diverse skills and perspectives. Born from the merger of two teams, we share one ambition: to tackle challenges, develop creative solutions, and push the boundaries of innovation together.
summary:
FarmPartner is a free farm advisor built on a trained AI engine that helps farmers adapt crop rotations to climate change, pests and soil depletion.

It works in any messaging app (WhatsApp, Messenger, iMessage, Instagram, Line, SMS). It currently runs on WhatsApp, and a desktop app is available at https://farmpartner.space.

It breaks language barriers with 46+ languages and promotes digital inclusion: farmers use text or voice, so no reading or writing is needed.

Farmers share a location, confirm crops detected from USDA maps and choose a goal. In 30 seconds, FarmPartner analyzes 20 years of NASA POWER, MODIS, GRACE, SMAP and ECOSTRESS data for that field, plus USDA soils and FAOSTAT. The engine is also trained with open data from around the world.

It compares the current rotation with alternatives, including seasonal second crops, by water use, soil health, erosion, pests, resilience, income and forage, explaining its reasoning, evidence, data gaps and local risks.

Powered by Claude, it answers questions on irrigation, frost and crops from photos or voice notes, drawing on a 3,663-trial meta-analysis and SARE handbooks. It never invents numbers.

Generational renewal: it gives new farmers farming know-how from day one, without replacing farmers’ judgment.
details:
How does it work?


FarmPartner is a farm advisor that anyone can access through any type of messaging app (WhatsApp, Messenger, iMessage, Instagram, LINE, SMS). It is currently fully functional on WhatsApp and in the browser at https://farmpartner.space/, and can easily be extended to other messaging platforms. The flow:

  1. Location, however the farmer has it: a WhatsApp pin, a Google or Apple Maps link, coordinates (decimal or degrees-minutes-seconds), a postcode in the farmer's country or a town name. Pins on open water, towns or forest are detected and the farmer is asked again.
  2. Field data in about 30 seconds: NASA and partner sources are fetched in parallel for that point. Only derived features are stored: rain vs. evaporation demand, frost dates, growing degree days, heat-stress days, bare-soil months, soil moisture, crop water stress and the long-term water-storage trend.
  3. Crops and goals: in the U.S. the current rotation is detected from nine years of USDA crop maps and the farmer just confirms it. Elsewhere the farmer types or says the crops in any language, or sends a photo, and FAOSTAT tells us what that country grows. Tree crops (olives, almonds, pistachios…) are set up as orchards. Goals: save water, soil health, income, less erosion or forage, several at once or in the farmer's own words.
  4. Rotation comparison: a deterministic, explainable engine scores today's rotation and the alternatives on seven sub-scores (water, soil, erosion, pest-cycle break, heat and drought resilience, income, forage). It searches every 2–3-year sequence of crops that fit the site, fills the gaps with seasonal second crops (double-crop soybeans or sorghum after wheat, grazed winter forage, cover crops) and ranks options by the farmer's goals and the overall score. Each option shows a season-by-season calendar, why it was suggested, the evidence and its source, benefits, information gaps and risks to check locally.
  5. Research behind every suggestion: expected yield gains from a meta-analysis of 3,663 field trials (Mudare et al. 2025, Nature Communications), long-term rotation experiments near the field (DRIVES), and a library of 2,991 passages from SARE handbooks and other guides that the AI cites by page.
  6. Ongoing help: farmers ask anything by text, voice note or crop photo ("should I water this week?", "is frost coming?") and get answers in their own language (English, Spanish, Basque, Japanese and more) and units (inches and °F or mm and °C). A daily job checks the forecast for frost, heat and irrigation alerts.

Data we use

NASA: POWER (MERRA-2 daily climate, 2006 to today), MODIS MOD13Q1 NDVI (250 m), SMAP L4 soil moisture (9 km) and ECOSTRESS evaporative stress index (70 m) through AppEEARS, and GRACE / GRACE-FO JPL mascons (water-storage and groundwater trend).

Other sources: USDA Cropland Data Layer and SSURGO soil survey, FAOSTAT crop statistics, Open-Meteo forecast, elevation and geocoding, GeoNames and the U.S. Census geocoder.

Tools and technologies

Python, FastAPI and SQLAlchemy; Supabase Postgres; Google Cloud Run, Cloud Storage and Cloud Scheduler, all defined in Terraform; Twilio WhatsApp Business API; Claude (Opus 5.5 for conversation and tool use, Haiku 5.5 for translation); Google Speech-to-Text for voice notes. Open source under the MIT licence.

Benefits and impact

Environmental: rotations that break pest cycles, keep the soil covered and use less water, with a warning where NASA GRACE shows a shrinking aquifer.

Economic: clearer crop decisions with expected yield effects, double-crop and forage opportunities, and the local market risks to check.

Accessibility: no app and no forms: a chat farmers already use, in their language, by text, voice or photo.

Digital inclusion: no app and no forms: a chat farmers already use, by text, voice note or photo, so no reading, writing or digital skills are needed.

No language barrier: FarmPartner works in over 46 languages, answering each farmer in their own language and units.

Generational renewal: new farmers get reliable, evidence-based guidance from day one, and the knowledge of experienced farmers is preserved and shared.

What makes FarmPartner different?

Every number comes from a named source: the AI explains and cites, it never invents. The engine is transparent and says out loud what the data can't see (POWER is a ~50 km grid, SMAP 9 km, GRACE ~300 km; crop maps cover only the U.S.). And it dares to go beyond standard rotations, while labelling new combinations so farmers try them on part of a field first.

Privacy by design: no AI model has access to users’ personal data, as all data are pseudonymized before processing. Farmers stay in control: writing “reset” at any time permanently deletes all their data. Otherwise, data are stored on our servers only for the period stated at https://farmpartner.space/privacy.

What do we hope to achieve?

Short term: validate the recommendations with farmers and agronomists in different regions, and calibrate the crop traits and scores.

Next: knowledge contributed by experienced farmers, local prices, climate-analogue regions (learning from places that already have your future climate), a farmer community, and full deployment on more channels (Messenger, iMessage, Instagram, LINE and SMS).

Long term: an open, accessible decision-support tool for farming communities worldwide.

FarmPartner supports, and does not replace, farmers' judgment and local agronomic expertise.
dataRefs: NASA POWER (MERRA-2 daily weather, rainfall, root-zone soil wetness)
NASA SMAP L4 soil moisture (SPL4SMGP, via AppEEARS)
NASA ECOSTRESS Evaporative Stress Index (ECO_L4T_ESI, via AppEEARS)
NASA MODIS MOD13Q1 NDVI 250 m (ORNL DAAC subsets)
NASA GRACE / GRACE-FO JPL mascon RL06.3 (water storage trend)
NASA AppEEARS (point extraction for SMAP and ECOSTRESS)
projectRefs: USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer (CropScape): crop history per field, 30 m
USDA NRCS Soil Data Access (SSURGO soil survey)
FAOSTAT Crops and livestock products (FAO, 2020-2024): main crops per country
Open-Meteo: 7-day forecast, elevation and place-name geocoding
GeoNames (CC BY 4.0): pin to country, offline
U.S. Census Bureau Geocoder: county names
Zippopotam.us: postal codes in many countries
Mudare et al. 2025, Crop rotations synergize yield, nutrition, and revenue: a meta-analysis (Nature Communications)
DRIVES long-term crop rotation experiments database (U.S., Canada, Mexico)
SARE handbook: Managing Cover Crops Profitably, 3rd ed. (agronomy library)
SARE handbook: Building Soils for Better Crops, 4th ed. (agronomy library)
SARE manual: Crop Rotation on Organic Farms (agronomy library)
Best4Soil (EU Horizon 2020): crop rotation practical guide (agronomy library)
Anthropic Claude (Opus 5.5, Haiku 5.5): conversation, tool use, translation, crop photos
Google Cloud Speech-to-Text: WhatsApp voice notes
